title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 2 of the third draft ('troisième mouture', Ch. VII, 23 June 1986) of Grothendieck's 'Analysis situs'. The previous page announced an axiomatisation of an 'algèbre des figures' or 'atelier'. These are purely algebraic axioms At1–At7, with topological properties (density, connectedness, acyclicity) and geometric ones (topological balls and spheres) deliberately excluded. A related notion, an atelier 'définissant une contrée', appears to be a region or domain carved out by the atelier.

On this page Grothendieck records a methodological decision from the previous draft (Ch. VI). The primitive notion should be the abstract 'figure', an element of a set 𝓕 carrying two order relations: inclusion ≤ and refinement ≪ (defined on the next page). The primitive should not be:
- the 'figure ensembliste' or 'multiplicité', that is, a subset of an ambient point-set; nor
- the 'lieu' or 'lieu ponctuel' / 'point'.
In modern terms he chooses a point-free, lattice- or mereology-style foundation for (tame) geometric topology, in the spirit of locales or region-based topology, rather than a point-set one.

His stated reason is the simplicity of the algebraic formalism: multiplicities and set-theoretic figures can themselves be treated as particular figures. A second reason, in the diagonal marginal note, is largely illegible. He then fixes notation for three ways of 'realising' an abstract figure F inside one of the multiplicities M:
1. F̃: the part of M corresponding to F, as an element of a poset ordered by ≤. The next page notes that this realisation is compatible with intersection, (F∩G)~ = F̃ ∩ G̃.
2. Mulomb(F), the 'grande multiombre': F read as a set-theoretic figure in M, i.e. presumably a set of subfigures or 'pieces' of M.
3. Omb(F), the 'grande ombre': the support (underlying point-set) of Mulomb(F).

The key observation is that F̃ and Mulomb(F) faithfully determine F, while the shadow Omb(F) almost never does: it remembers only the support. The next page introduces the parallel 'small' versions, multombre(F) and ombre(F), relative to the set of lieux L. It then begins the data (𝓕, ≤, ≪) with Ax0 (F≤G ⇒ F≪G) and the operations ∨, ∧ (= Inf for ≤), the fine intersection F·G (= Inf for ≪), and the empty figure.

The problem served is a foundation for 'topologie modérée' (tame topology), announced in the Esquisse d'un programme §5. The aim is a formalism where finer structures than point-sets (e.g. stratifications or decompositions) are primitive, and point-sets appear only as lossy 'shadows'.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. It is notation and methodology, not proof. The claim that Omb(F) 'practically never' allows reconstructing F is informal but plausible: distinct figures, e.g. different decompositions or refinements, share the same support. This is consistent with the distinction between ≤ and ≪ introduced on the next page.

ideas.what: Taking abstract 'figures' as primitive, with points/lieux and set-theoretic figures as derived, to found tame/geometric topology algebraically.
ideas.modern_name: Point-free topology / mereotopology (region-based topology, contact algebras); locales.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna, Tarski (region-based geometry, 1920s–30s); Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone (locales, 1950s–80s).
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (1984), without this point-free axiomatics.

ideas.what: Distinguishing an abstract figure F from its realisations: as part F̃ of a multiplicity, as set-theoretic 'multi-shadow' Mulomb(F), and as support Omb(F), with only the support being lossy.
ideas.modern_name: Faithful vs. forgetful realisation functors; a decomposition/stratification versus its underlying set (support of a cycle or stratified set).
ideas.usually_credited_to: No single source; analogous to support of cycles/sheaves, and in o-minimality cell decompositions versus definable sets (van den Dries).

ideas.what: Atelier ('workshop') / contrée terminology for an algebra of figures and the region it defines.
ideas.modern_name: Lattice-ordered algebra of regions; abstract tame structure.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's tame-topology programme was, in its 1986 third draft, explicitly reformulated point-free: figures with inclusion and refinement orders are primitive, and point-sets are mere 'shadows'. This links Esquisse §5 to mereotopology/contact algebras and locale theory, a connection the o-minimality and tame-topology literature (which is point-set based) did not take up.
missed.quote: La notion fondamentale me semble bien celle de figure, et non pas celle de "figure ensembliste" ou "multiplicité", voire celle de "lieu"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A point-free axiomatics of tame topology, with a refinement order alongside inclusion, could interface o-minimal geometry with region-based theories and with formal/constructive topology. No such synthesis appears in the standard literature.

missed.claim: The 'grande/petite multiombre' and 'ombre' realisation maps from abstract figures to set-theoretic figures, and the question of when an abstract figure is reconstructible from its realisations, are set up but not developed here.
missed.quote: cette dernière, contrairement à F̃ et à Mulomb(F), ne permettant pratiquement jamais de reconstituer F
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This amounts to a representation-theorem question (Stone-type) for algebras of figures. That kind of question is studied for contact algebras, but not for Grothendieck's ateliers.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly foundational notation. Still, the explicit point-free stance of Grothendieck's unpublished tame-topology axiomatics, with set-theoretic figures as 'shadows', is a little-known design decision that is absent from the published record. The notes are, however, unfinished and at an early stage.
transcription_corrections: Interlinear addition above 'interprétée comme' reads approximately '(par l'un de ses "objets")' and is uncertain; the parenthetical '(ordonnée par ≤)' sits below 'interprétée' and qualifies the 'partie'.
'Quand elle est interprétée comme une figure ensembliste dans M': 'ensembliste' is an interlinear insertion above 'dans M'.
The final line ends roughly '... mais seulement, son "support" seulement', i.e. the shadow recovers only the support of F. The struck word after 'reconstituer F,' is illegible.
Diagonal left-margin note begins 'L'autre raison: car d'une "multiplicité" ...' and seems to mention 'figures multiplicités'; mostly illegible.
